claim: AXL is induced in response to type I interferons (IFNs).
source: The receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) AXL is induced in response to type I interferons (IFNs) and limits their production through a negative feedback loop.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about AXL function.

claim: AXL limits type I IFN production through a negative feedback loop.
source: The receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) AXL is induced in response to type I interferons (IFNs) and limits their production through a negative feedback loop.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about AXL function.

claim: Enhanced production of type I IFNs occurs in Axl-/- dendritic cells (DCs) in vitro.
source: Enhanced production of type I IFNs in Axl-/- dendritic cells (DCs) in vitro have led to speculation that inhibition of AXL would promote antiviral responses.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Ablation of AXL enhances susceptibility to infection by influenza A virus.
source: Here we demonstrate that ablation of AXL enhances the susceptibility to infection by influenza A virus and West Nile virus.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by survival data in Figure 1A.

claim: Ablation of AXL enhances susceptibility to infection by West Nile virus.
source: Here we demonstrate that ablation of AXL enhances the susceptibility to infection by influenza A virus and West Nile virus.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: The increased type I IFN response in Axl-/- mice was associated with diminished DC maturation.
source: The increased type I IFN response in Axl-/- mice was associated with diminished DC maturation, reduced production of IL-1β, and defective antiviral T cell immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3A and 3B showing reduced MHC-I and MHC-II expression.

claim: The increased type I IFN response in Axl-/- mice was associated with reduced production of IL-1β.
source: The increased type I IFN response in Axl-/- mice was associated with diminished DC maturation, reduced production of IL-1β, and defective antiviral T cell immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3C, 3D, and Figure 8A.

claim: The increased type I IFN response in Axl-/- mice was associated with defective antiviral T cell immunity.
source: The increased type I IFN response in Axl-/- mice was associated with diminished DC maturation, reduced production of IL-1β, and defective antiviral T cell immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Blockade of type I IFN receptor restored the antiviral adaptive response in Axl-/- mice.
source: Blockade of type I IFN receptor or administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored the antiviral adaptive response and control of infection.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: Administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored the antiviral adaptive response and control of infection.
source: Blockade of type I IFN receptor or administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored the antiviral adaptive response and control of infection.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 8C, 8D, and 8E.

claim: AXL is essential for limiting the immunosuppressive effects of type I IFNs.
source: Our results demonstrate that AXL is essential for limiting the immunosuppressive effects of type I IFNs and enabling the induction of protective antiviral adaptive immunity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the experimental findings.

claim: AXL is essential for enabling the induction of protective antiviral adaptive immunity.
source: Our results demonstrate that AXL is essential for limiting the immunosuppressive effects of type I IFNs and enabling the induction of protective antiviral adaptive immunity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the experimental findings.

claim: AXL is a member of the TAM (TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK) subfamily of RTK.
source: AXL is a member of the TAM (TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK) subfamily of RTK that potently inhibits the production of type I IFNs (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013; Rothlin et al., 2015; Rothlin et al., 2007; Zagorska et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TAM receptors potently inhibit the production of type I IFNs.
source: AXL is a member of the TAM (TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK) subfamily of RTK that potently inhibits the production of type I IFNs (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013; Rothlin et al., 2015; Rothlin et al., 2007; Zagorska et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: AXL is an IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) in DCs.
source: In DCs, AXL is an IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) and hijacks molecular components of type I IFN signaling to induce the expression of Suppressor of Cytokine Signaling (SOCS) 1 and SOCS3 (Rothlin et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: AXL hijacks molecular components of type I IFN signaling to induce the expression of SOCS1 and SOCS3.
source: In DCs, AXL is an IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) and hijacks molecular components of type I IFN signaling to induce the expression of Suppressor of Cytokine Signaling (SOCS) 1 and SOCS3 (Rothlin et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SOCS1 and SOCS3 downregulate type I IFN signaling.
source: SOCS1 and SOCS3, in turn, downregulate type I IFN signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: AXL is a key component of a homeostatic mechanism that controls type I IFN levels.
source: Therefore, AXL is a key component of a homeostatic mechanism that controls type I IFN levels.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the previous statements.

claim: AXL has been identified as an enhancer of infection by enveloped viruses in vitro.
source: Recent studies using an array of enveloped viruses have identified AXL as an enhancer of infection in vitro, including in DCs (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013; Meertens et al., 2012; Morizono et al., 2011; Shimojima et al., 2007; 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Enveloped viruses exploit apoptotic mimicry by exposing phosphatidylserine on their lipid envelopes.
source: Enveloped viruses exploit apoptotic mimicry by exposing phosphatidylserine on their lipid envelopes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Binding of phosphatidylserine to GAS6 leads to the activation of AXL on host cells.
source: Binding of phosphatidylserine to the AXL agonist growth arrest-specific 6 (GAS6) protein leads to the activation of AXL on host cells (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013; Lew et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Activation of AXL through viral apoptotic mimicry leads to the induction of Socs genes and suppression of type I IFN production and signaling.
source: Activation of AXL through viral apoptotic mimicry leads to the induction of the Socs genes and the suppression of type I IFN production and signaling (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The non-enveloped virus SV40 can engage AXL directly by structural mimicry to facilitate infection.
source: It was also shown that the non-enveloped virus SV40 can engage AXL directly by structural mimicry to facilitate infection (Drayman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Type I IFNs were identified based on their ability to inhibit the propagation of viruses.
source: Type I IFNs were identified based on their ability to inhibit the propagation of viruses (Isaacs and Lindenmann, 1957; Taniguchi et al., 1980).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Genetic ablation of Axl resulted in enhanced production and signaling of type I IFN during viral infection of cells in vitro.
source: Accordingly, genetic ablation of Axl resulted in an enhanced production and signaling of type I IFN during viral infection of cells in vitro and increased the resistance of DCs to the virus (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Genetic ablation of Axl increased the resistance of DCs to virus in vitro.
source: Accordingly, genetic ablation of Axl resulted in an enhanced production and signaling of type I IFN during viral infection of cells in vitro and increased the resistance of DCs to the virus (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Sustained production of type I IFNs during chronic LCMV infection inhibited the generation of virus-specific T cells and prevented viral clearance.
source: For example, sustained production of type I IFNs during chronic lymphocytic choriomeningitis (LCMV) infection inhibited the generation of virus-specific T cells and prevented viral clearance (Teijaro et al., 2013; Wilson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Type I IFNs inhibit protective cell-intrinsic responses against intracellular bacteria, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
source: In particular, type I IFNs inhibit protective cell-intrinsic responses against intracellular bacteria, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mayer-Barber et al., 2010; 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Immunosuppressive effects of type I IFNs may underlie their pharmacological efficacy in the treatment of multiple sclerosis.
source: Additionally, immunosuppressive effects of type I IFNs may underlie their pharmacological efficacy in the treatment of multiple sclerosis (Prinz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: By 11 days after intranasal administration of PR8, significantly more Axl-/- mice than WT mice succumbed to the infection.
source: By 11 days after intranasal administration of PR8, significantly more Axl-/- mice than WT mice succumbed to the infection (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the survival curve in Figure 1A.

claim: The increased susceptibility of Axl-/- mice to IAV infection is in agreement with a report by Fujimori et al.
source: This result is in agreement with a recent report by Fujimori et al (Fujimori et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: The increased susceptibility of Axl-/- mice to IAV infection correlated with higher viral titers in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid than in WT mice 7 and 9 days post-infection.
source: The increased susceptibility of Axl-/- mice to IAV infection correlated with higher viral titers in the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid than in WT mice 7 and 9 days post-infection (Figure 1B), corresponding to when the CD8+ T cell response is critical in viral clearance.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: No significant differences in viral loads were detected during the early phase of infection (day 3 post-infection) between WT and Axl-/- mice.
source: However, no significant differences in viral loads were detected during the early phase of the infection between WT and Axl-/- mice (day 3 post-infection, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: AXL is expressed in both CD11c+CD11b+CD103- and CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DC subsets during influenza infection.
source: Flow cytometry analyses revealed that AXL is expressed in both of these DC subsets during influenza infection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: AXL ablation did not affect the total number of CD11c+CD11b+CD103- and CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs in the lung.
source: Importantly, AXL ablation did not affect the total number of CD11c+CD11b+CD103- and CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs in the lung (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Significantly fewer infected CD11c+CD11b+CD103- DCs were detected in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice.
source: When PR8-GFP infected Axl-/- mice were compared to WT mice, we detected significantly fewer infected CD11c+CD11b+CD103- DCs (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Fewer GFP+ CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs were identified in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice.
source: Likewise, fewer GFP+ CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs were identified in Axl-/- mice (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Axl-/- and WT alveolar macrophages were equally susceptible to infection by PR8-GFP.
source: Axl-/- and WT alveolar macrophages were equally susceptible to infection by PR8-GFP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Alveolar macrophages express both AXL and MERTK.
source: Alveolar macrophages express both AXL and the related receptor MERTK, while only AXL but not MERTK was detected on lung DCs (Fujimori et al., 2015) and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Only AXL but not MERTK was detected on lung DCs.
source: Alveolar macrophages express both AXL and the related receptor MERTK, while only AXL but not MERTK was detected on lung DCs (Fujimori et al., 2015) and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Axl-/- BMDCs were significantly more resistant to infection by PR8-GFP than WT BMDCs.
source: Similar to a previous report using pseudotyped HIV-1 and WNV (Bhattacharyya et al., 2013), Axl-/- BMDCs were significantly more resistant to infection by PR8-GFP than WT BMDCs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The abundance of PR8 polymerase acidic protein transcript in Axl-/- BMDCs was lower than in WT BMDC cultures.
source: Additionally, the abundance of transcript of PR8 polymerase acidic protein (PA) in Axl-/- BMDCs was lower than in WT BMDC cultures (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: AXL is a well-established phagocytic receptor that mediates the engulfment of apoptotic cells.
source: AXL is a well-established phagocytic receptor that mediates the engulfment of apoptotic cells (Rothlin et al., 2015; Zagorska et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Reduced percentages of M2+Axl-/- BMDCs were detected in comparison to M2+ WT BMDCs throughout the range of tested MOIs of PR8-GFP.
source: We detected reduced percentages of M2+Axl-/- BMDCs in comparison to M2+ WT BMDCs throughout the range of tested MOIs of PR8-GFP (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: Significantly lower amounts of MHC-I and MHC-II were measured on CD11c+CD11b+CD103- DCs in the draining MLN in Axl-/- mice 72 hr post-infection with IAV.
source: Significantly lower amounts of MHC-I and MHC-II were measured on CD11c+CD11b+CD103- DCs in the draining MLN in Axl-/- mice 72 hr post-infection with IAV (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: Reduced expression of MHC-I and MHC-II was observed in Axl-/- CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ cells.
source: The reduced expression of MHC-I and MHC-II was also observed in Axl-/- CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: IL-1β is required for effective activation of lung dendritic cells and induction of adaptive immunity during IAV infection.
source: IL-1β has been shown to be required for effective activation of lung dendritic cells and induction of adaptive immunity during IAV infection (Pang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: Significantly fewer IL-1β-producing CD11c+CD11b+CD103- DCs were found in the lung of Axl-/- mice 72 hr post-infection compared to WT mice.
source: We found significantly fewer IL-1β-producing CD11c+CD11b+CD103- and CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs in the lung of Axl-/- mice 72 hr post-infection in comparison to WT mice (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: Significantly fewer IL-1β-producing CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs were found in the lung of Axl-/- mice 72 hr post-infection compared to WT mice.
source: We found significantly fewer IL-1β-producing CD11c+CD11b+CD103- and CD11c+CD11b-CD103+ DCs in the lung of Axl-/- mice 72 hr post-infection in comparison to WT mice (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: Alveolar macrophages from both infected WT and Axl-/- mice produced equal amounts of IL-1β.
source: In contrast, alveolar macrophages from both infected WT and Axl-/- mice produced equal amounts of IL-1β (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3E.

claim: Cd11c-Cre+ Axlfl/fl mice succumbed at a higher frequency to PR8 than Cd11c-Cre-Axlfl/fl control mice.
source: Analogous to that seen in Axl-/- mice, Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice succumbed at a higher frequency to PR8 than Cd11c-Cre-Axlfl/fl control mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: Csf1r-Cre+ Axlfl/fl mice were as resistant to IAV infection as control mice.
source: In contrast, Csf1r-Cre+ Axlfl/fl were as resistant to IAV infection as control mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: The ablation of AXL in myeloid cells is sufficient to confer susceptibility to IAV infection.
source: Take together, these results indicate that the ablation of AXL in myeloid cells is sufficient to confer susceptibility to IAV infection and that preserved expression in DCs appears to be required to resist the infection.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the conditional knockout experiments.

claim: Preserved expression of AXL in DCs appears to be required to resist IAV infection.
source: Take together, these results indicate that the ablation of AXL in myeloid cells is sufficient to confer susceptibility to IAV infection and that preserved expression in DCs appears to be required to resist the infection.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the conditional knockout experiments.

claim: Expression of CD69 was significantly lower in draining MLN CD8+ T cells in Axl-/- mice compared to WT controls 3 days post-infection with PR8.
source: Expression of CD69, an early T cell activation marker, was significantly lower in draining MLN CD8+ T cells in Axl-/- mice in comparison to WT controls 3 days post-infection with PR8 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lung CD8+ T cells showed diminished production of IFN-γ 9 days post infection in Axl-/- mice.
source: Lung CD8+ T cells also showed a diminished production of IFN-γ 9 days post infection (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: The number of IFN-γ+ antigen-restricted CD8+ T cells specific for IAV PA amino acids 224–233 was reduced in the lung of Axl-/- mice.
source: The number of IFN-γ+ antigen-restricted CD8+ T cells specific for IAV PA amino acids 224–233 was similarly reduced in the lung of Axl-/- mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: The number of CD8+CD44+ cells in the MLN was less in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice.
source: Furthermore, as an additional marker of activation, the number of CD8+CD44+ cells in the MLN as well as the expression level of CD44 on CD8+ T cells in the lung was less in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The expression level of CD44 on CD8+ T cells in the lung was less in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice.
source: Furthermore, as an additional marker of activation, the number of CD8+CD44+ cells in the MLN as well as the expression level of CD44 on CD8+ T cells in the lung was less in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: CD4+ T cells in Axl-/- mice were less activated as evidenced by their reduced expression of IFN-γ and CD44.
source: Similarly, CD4+ T cells in Axl-/- mice were less activated as evidenced by their reduced expression of IFN-γ and CD44 (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice had significantly fewer IFN-γ producing CD8+ T cells compared to controls.
source: As was seen in Axl-/- mice, Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl but not Cd11c-Cre-Axlfl/fl had significantly fewer number of IFN-γ producing CD8+ T cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice had lower numbers of PA-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: This reduction was in part due to lower numbers of PA-specific CD8+ T cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Csf1r-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice had preserved CD8+ T cell responses.
source: In contrast, Csf1r-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice had preserved CD8+ T cell responses. (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice developed fewer IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells compared to respective controls.
source: Similarly, Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice developed fewer IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells in comparison to respective controls, while this response was conserved in Csf1r-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: The CD4+ T cell response was conserved in Csf1r-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice.
source: Similarly, Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice developed fewer IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells in comparison to respective controls, while this response was conserved in Csf1r-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Myeloid-specific ablation of AXL in Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice is sufficient to account for the impaired T cell activation phenotype seen in complete Axl-/- mice.
source: These results indicate that myeloid-specific ablation of AXL in Cd11c-Cre+Axlfl/fl mice is sufficient to account for the impaired T cell activation phenotype seen in complete Axl-/- mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the conditional knockout experiments.

claim: Axl-/- mice developed deficient CD8+ T cell responses to WNV.
source: As seen during IAV infection, Axl-/- mice developed deficient CD8+ T cell responses to WNV.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: The percentage and number of NS4B tetramer+ cells were reduced in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice after WNV infection.
source: The percentage and number of NS4B tetramer+ cells (Figure 6A) and IFN-γ-producing CD8+ T cells (Figure 6B) were reduced in Axl-/- mice in comparison to WT mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: IFN-γ-producing CD8+ T cells were reduced in Axl-/- mice compared to WT mice after WNV infection.
source: The percentage and number of NS4B tetramer+ cells (Figure 6A) and IFN-γ-producing CD8+ T cells (Figure 6B) were reduced in Axl-/- mice in comparison to WT mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: Levels of intracellular granzyme B were reduced in both NS4B tetramer+Axl-/- CD8+ T cells and total Axl-/- CD8+ T cell populations after WNV infection.
source: Similarly, levels of intracellular granzyme B were reduced in both NS4B tetramer+Axl-/- CD8+ T cells and total Axl-/- CD8+ T cell populations (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: The WNV findings are in agreement with the increased susceptibility of Axl-/- mice to WNV infection.
source: These results are in agreement with the increased susceptibility of Axl-/- mice to WNV infection (Miner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: Loss of AXL signaling leads to a defect in priming the adaptive antiviral T cell responses after IAV and WNV infections.
source: Collectively, these results show that loss of AXL signaling leads to a defect in priming the adaptive antiviral T cell responses after IAV and WNV infections.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Increased production of IFN-β was detected in IAV-infected Axl-/- versus WT BMDC cultures.
source: We detected increased production of IFN-β in IAV-infected Axl-/- versus WT BMDC cultures (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 7A.

claim: Neutralization of type I IFN signaling by MAR1-5A3 anti-IFNAR antibody restored the susceptibility of Axl-/- BMDCs to PR8 infection.
source: Furthermore, neutralization of type I IFN signaling by MAR1-5A3 anti-IFNAR antibody restored the susceptibility of Axl-/- BMDCs to PR8 infection (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 7B.

claim: A significant increase in the survival of IAV-infected Axl-/- mice treated with MAR1-5A3 was detected.
source: We detected a significant increase in the survival of IAV-infected Axl-/- mice treated with MAR1-5A3 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 7C.

claim: Treatment with anti-type I IFN receptor antibody restored IFN-γ+ PA-restricted CD8+ T cells in infected Axl-/- mice.
source: This correlated with a restoration of IFN-γ+ PA-restricted CD8+ T cells and IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 7D.

claim: Treatment with anti-type I IFN receptor antibody restored IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells in infected Axl-/- mice.
source: This correlated with a restoration of IFN-γ+ PA-restricted CD8+ T cells and IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 7D.

claim: The number of CD8+CD44+ and CD4+CD44+ T cells in infected Axl-/- mice treated with anti-type I IFN receptor antibody were restored to that of control mice.
source: Similarly, the number of CD8+CD44+ and CD4+CD44+ T cells in infected Axl-/- mice treated with the anti-type I IFN receptor antibody were restored to that of control mice (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 7D.

claim: The increased production of IFN-β in IAV-infected Axl-/- BMDCs correlated with a concomitant reduction in the production of IL-1β.
source: The increased production of IFN-β in IAV-infected Axl-/- BMDCs correlated with a concomitant reduction in the production of IL-1β (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 8A.

claim: Neutralization of type I IFN signaling in infected Axl-/- BMDCs rescued IL-1β production by these cells.
source: Furthermore, neutralization of type I IFN signaling in infected Axl-/- BMDCs rescued IL-1β production by these cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 8B.

claim: Axl-/- mice that were given IL-1β were completely protected and survived IAV infection.
source: Axl-/- mice that were given IL-1β were completely protected and survived the infection (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 8C.

claim: Viral titers in the BALF of Axl-/- mice given IL-1β were controlled to the level of WT controls.
source: Consistent with this protection, viral titers in the BALF of Axl-/- mice given IL-1β were controlled to the level of WT controls (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 8D.

claim: The administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored the antiviral adaptive immune response as measured by the number of IFN-γ+ PA-restricted CD8+ T cells and IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells.
source: Furthermore, the administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored the antiviral adaptive immune response as measured by the number of IFN-γ+ PA-restricted CD8+ T cells and IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells (Figure 8E) as well as CD8+CD44+ and CD4+CD44+ T cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 8E.

claim: The administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored CD8+CD44+ and CD4+CD44+ T cells.
source: Furthermore, the administration of IL-1β to Axl-/- mice restored the antiviral adaptive immune response as measured by the number of IFN-γ+ PA-restricted CD8+ T cells and IFN-γ producing CD4+ T cells (Figure 8E) as well as CD8+CD44+ and CD4+CD44+ T cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The genetic ablation of Axl leads to enhanced production of type I IFNs and decreased production of IL-1β resulting in impaired induction of antiviral adaptive immunity and clearance of virus.
source: In summary, these results demonstrate that the genetic ablation of Axl leads to enhanced production of type I IFNs and decreased production of IL-1β resulting in impaired induction of antiviral adaptive immunity and clearance of virus.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Mice featuring the genetic ablation of Axl are more susceptible to viral infection than WT mice.
source: In direct opposition to this hypothesis, our experimental evidence demonstrates that mice featuring the genetic ablation of Axl, even after selective deletion in myeloid cells, are more susceptible to viral infection than WT mice.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the main finding.

claim: Loss of Axl leads to a reduced ability to mount an adequate adaptive antiviral response.
source: We report that loss of Axl leads to a reduced ability to mount an adequate adaptive antiviral response, as exemplified by deficient priming of T cells after IAV and WNV infection.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The phenotype of deficient T cell priming in Axl-/- mice is consistent with previous findings on the susceptibility to IAV infection of mice lacking CD8+ T cells.
source: This phenotype is consistent with previous findings on the susceptibility to IAV infection of mice lacking CD8+ T cells (Bender et al., 1992; Wu et al., 2010).

claim: The ability of AXL to inhibit type I IFN production appears to be important for induction of antiviral adaptive immunity.
